title: Founding Quantum Fund with Jim Rogers
statement: After his Arrow/DoubleClick-era work and a fractious split from F.M. Mayer, Soros set up his own shop and then the Quantum Fund, applying the philosophy of reflexivity he had developed as a student under Karl Popper to markets.
outcome: Quantum returned roughly 30% annually over its first two decades and became one of the most successful funds in history, making Soros a billionaire and financing his open-society philanthropy.

title: Shorting sterling ahead of Black Wednesday
statement: Recognizing that Britain's ERM peg was unsustainable given German interest rates and the UK's inflation, Soros built a short position reported at roughly $10 billion across Quantum and other accounts, prepared to hold through political pressure.
outcome: On September 16, 1992 the Bank of England withdrew from the ERM and let sterling float; Quantum's profit was reported at approximately $1 billion in a single day, and Soros became known as 'the man who broke the Bank of England.'

title: Writing 'The Alchemy of Finance' and formalizing reflexivity
statement: Soros codified his theory that market prices do not passively reflect fundamentals but actively shape them — bias affects fundamentals which affect bias — and published an experiment-rich account of applying the theory in real time.
outcome: The book became required reading for macro traders and reframed how a generation of practitioners thought about bubbles and disequilibrium markets.

title: Southeast Asian currency shorts during the 1997 crisis
statement: As Thai baht and regional pegs came under pressure from dollar-pegged overvalued exchange rates and short-term dollar debt, Quantum and other macro funds ran short positions against the currencies.
outcome: The baht float of July 2, 1997 began the Asian financial crisis; Malaysia's PM Mahathir publicly accused Soros of destabilizing the region, though the role of fundamentals remains the mainstream explanation. The episode made Soros a political figure in Asia.

title: Losing $2 billion in the Russia default while the Russia fund still profited
statement: Quantum had a substantial long position in Russian assets going into the August 1998 default and devaluation, which Soros had publicly warned about — but had not fully exited in time; the loss approached $2 billion at the fund level.
outcome: The episode demonstrated the gap between his macro thesis and his fund's positioning; the dedicated Russia fund itself closed with roughly 30% annualized returns for its life. Soros called it one of his most painful lessons about acting on one's own analysis.

title: Doubling down on tech into the 2000 top after Druckenmiller's warning
statement: In early 2000, against the advice of Stanley Druckenmiller who had exited tech, Soros increased Quantum's technology exposure, expecting the rally to continue long enough to exit later.
outcome: Quantum fell roughly 22% in the first months of 2000; Soros publicly admitted the mistake, replaced his management, and moved Quantum into a safer, lower-return vehicle — publicly saying 'maybe I don't understand the market anymore.'

title: Open Society Foundations — building the philanthropy at scale
statement: Soros consolidated his giving into the Open Society Foundations, applying Popper's open-society philosophy — that no one has a monopoly on truth and institutions must allow error correction — first in Eastern Europe and then globally.
outcome: OSF has disbursed over $19 billion across more than 120 countries, making Soros one of the largest philanthropists in history and the model of ideology-driven mega-giving.

title: 2008 crash — going from cautious to aggressively long after September
statement: After protecting capital through the Lehman disintegration, Soros returned to active management of his own account in the fourth quarter of 2008, buying equities aggressively at the lows.
outcome: His fund reportedly gained roughly 8% in 2009 on these positions, and Soros wrote that the episode vindicated both his reflexivity framework — the crash was a textbook reflexive bust — and the discipline of re-engaging after certainty collapsed.

title: Pledging $1 billion to OSI-style university networks
statement: At the age of 90, Soros committed $1 billion to founding the Open Society University Network, a global network of teaching institutions to advance open-society values.
outcome: The pledge was among the largest single gifts in the history of higher education philanthropy.

title: Handing Soros Fund Management to family-office-only status
statement: Citing new regulatory reporting requirements under Dodd-Frank and the strain of managing outside capital, Soros returned all outside money and converted his firm to a family office.
outcome: The conversion preserved the capital base for the family and the Foundations; the step was followed within months by other legendary managers including Stanley Druckenmiller and Carl Icahn.
